slide.title: A theme file, validated then applied
slide.takeaway: theme.css at the Saga root may only override tokens; a strict parser re-serializes what it accepts, and the reviewer applies it after its defaults and inside every served slide.

item.label: theme.css at the Saga root
item.description: A Saga holds at most one theme, at a fixed name beside saga.json; Load reads it, and a Saga without one has none.

item.label: A strict parser, reported by validate
item.description: Comments are blanked, keeping lines; forbidden constructs are refused outright; only the two blocks and contract tokens pass. Each problem names its line, and validate reports it at theme.css:LINE.

item.label: Values by token kind
item.description: Each value must parse as its token's kind and is re-serialized from the parse: colours to hex, lengths, font lists, and shadows rebuilt from their parts.

item.label: The app links /theme.css
item.description: The theme emits its overrides for light and both routes to dark; the reviewer serves them at /theme.css after app.css, so page markup and its caches do not change with the theme.

item.label: Served slides carry the tokens
item.description: Each SVG or HTML slide is served with one style at its end declaring every token, resolved per scheme with the theme applied, so var(--token) and generated slides follow it.

item.label: An invalid theme is not applied at all
item.description: The reviewer drops the whole theme when any line is invalid.
item.body: You might expect the valid lines of a broken theme to apply; instead the reviewer keeps its defaults until the file validates, so a half-applied theme never ships unnoticed. validate and theme check name what to fix.

item.label: A theme alone keeps a Saga review first
item.description: theme.css joins the review-only top-level entries.
item.body: Any other top-level entry makes a Saga count as living documentation; theme.css is listed with saga.json and README.md so adding a theme does not switch a reviews-only Saga to the full report.
